types.name: EShadingModel
types.doc:
Explicit surface shading model (G2). Values are the GBuffer wire IDs
(RT3.A bits 5..7) — renumbering breaks every already-rendered frame's
decode AND the CPU codec tests. 0 must remain DefaultLit: impostors,
decal-neutral writes and material-less draws all emit a zero alpha.

members.name: DefaultLit
members.doc: GGX; also "legacy auto" — derives Hair/Subsurface from the old scalar knobs

members.name: Unlit
members.doc: emissive passthrough, lighting skipped entirely

members.name: Subsurface
members.doc: Penner wrap-diffuse, strength in the custom lane, blurred by the SSS pass

members.name: ClearCoat
members.doc: second specular lobe (intensity/roughness keep their RT3 R/G lanes)

members.name: Hair
members.doc: Kajiya-Kay strands over the aniso tangent frame

members.name: TwoSidedFoliage
members.doc: adds albedo-tinted back-light transmission, strength in the custom lane

members.name: Cloth
members.doc: Charlie sheen lobe over the base diffuse — velvet, felt, brushed fabric

members.name: ThinTranslucent
members.doc:
Coloured glass: the surface TINTS what is behind it by Beer-Lambert
absorption instead of fading it. Transmission strength is the thickness.
NOTE: this fills the classic tier of RT3.A's surface code (0-6 plus this
one). Ids past it go through tier 7's escape, which names an extended
slot and moves that surface's payload to RT3.R/G — see FSurfaceCode.

members.name: Eye
members.doc:
The first EXTENDED model — it rides tier 7's escape, so RT3.R/G stop
being the clear coat's lanes and become a 16-bit record index into the
frame's surface-parameter buffer. Eye is the model that forced the
indirection: its defining input is a per-pixel iris normal, a float3
that no packed lane of any width was ever going to carry.

types.name: FEyeSurfaceParams
types.doc:
Eye's surface parameters. None of them reach the G-Buffer directly — the
renderer writes one FSurfaceRecord per drawn Eye material into the frame's
surface-parameter buffer and RT3 stores only that record's index, which is
what buys a lit pixel a whole struct instead of five bits.

members.name: IrisTint
members.doc:
Linear multiplier on the iris diffuse seen THROUGH the cornea. Kept
separate from base color so a single albedo texture can cover sclera
and iris while only the iris takes the tint.

members.name: CorneaIoR
members.doc:
Refractive index of the cornea (~1.376 in vivo). It sets both the
corneal Fresnel and how far the view ray bends before it reaches the
iris — the bend is the whole reason the iris needs its own normal.

members.name: IrisDepth
members.doc:
Anterior-chamber depth in world units: how far the iris sits behind the
corneal surface. 0 collapses the eye to a painted sphere, because
nothing is left for the refraction to travel through.

members.name: IrisConcavity
members.doc:
How far the iris has flattened out of the cornea's curvature, 0..1.
0 shades the iris with the corneal normal (indistinguishable from
DefaultLit); 1 faces it straight down the refracted ray.

members.name: GazeAxis
members.doc:
The eyeball's LOCAL pupil axis. Every field above is shared by every
draw of the material; this one is not, because the renderer transforms
it by each draw's own model matrix. That is the whole reason the record
is keyed per draw: two eyeballs on one material differ only by their
transform, and a material-keyed record made both eyes stare the same
way no matter where the heads were looking.

members.name: IrisConeDegrees
members.doc:
Half-angle of the iris disc about the gaze axis, in degrees, measured
from the eyeball's pivot. 0 disables the mask and the whole escaped
surface is iris — exactly what shipped before the mask existed, which
is why it is the default.

members.name: LimbalWidthDegrees
members.doc:
Angular width of the limbal transition in degrees: the iris fades out
across it and the ring darkens within it. Never applied at zero width —
a hard angular step aliases along the limbus at any resolution.

members.name: LimbalDarkening
members.doc:
Absorption in the limbal band, 0..1. 0 leaves the surface untouched, so
an eye authored before the ring existed is unmoved.

members.name: IrisRoughness
members.doc:
Roughness of the iris' OWN specular lobe, behind the cornea. 0 disables
it: the iris shipped diffuse-only, and a lobe that appeared by default
would move every existing eye.

members.name: CausticStrength
members.doc:
Light the corneal lens focuses onto the iris — the bright crescent
opposite a key light. 0 = off.

types.name: FWorldGridParams
types.doc:
The world-aligned procedural grid (UE's WorldGridMaterial). It is drawn by
the uber GBuffer shader from the pixel's world position and needs no texture
and no cooked graph shader, which is why it can be the material every mesh
without one falls back to. Base colour fills the cells; the shades multiply
it on the lines, so one value under 1 darkens the lines and one over 1
brightens them.

types.name: EMaterialBlendMode
types.doc:
How a TRANSLUCENT surface combines with the scene behind it. Opaque and
masked surfaces are expressed by opacity + alphaMasked and never reach
here. Values are serialized by index — append only.

members.name: Alpha
members.doc: src over dst — what every translucent did before this existed

members.name: Additive
members.doc: dst + src: fire, glows, holograms

members.name: Modulate
members.doc: dst * src: stained glass, smoked plastic

members.name: EyeParams
members.doc:
The last free bit, so Eye's five parameters share ONE override: they
are a single surface's description and are always authored together.

types.name: FMaterialIdentity
types.doc:
Process-unique material identity. Copies mint a FRESH id (a copy is a new
material object), assignment keeps the target's own — so an id never names
two live materials and, unlike the raw address it replaced as the DS-cache
key, is never reused after a delete (address reuse handed a new material
the previous occupant's cached descriptor set: wrong textures).

types.name: FMaterialTransparentDepth
types.doc:
Nesting depth of Material::FTransparentWriteScope. Copying a material never
copies an in-flight scope: the scope belongs to the operation running on the
ORIGINAL, and a render proxy that inherited a non-zero count would stop
recording override bits for the rest of its life.

types.name: FMaterialStateVersion
types.doc:
Count of surface changes on ONE material object, moved by every setter. The
render-proxy cache reuses last frame's snapshot while (identity, version)
still match, so a copy that carried the source's count would let a material
that was just overwritten by CopyFrom/ResetInPlace keep matching a snapshot
of what it used to be. Copying therefore never transfers it.

types.name: FMaterialState
types.doc:
Everything a material IS, kept apart from the object that carries the
reference count. Material derives from RefCounted, whose count must never be
copied — but the render proxy still snapshots a surface every frame and
Clone() still needs a field-wise duplicate. Holding the surface in a plainly
copyable base is what lets both of those exist without a hand-written
member list that silently skips the next field somebody adds.

members.name: m_metallic
members.doc: 0 = dielectric, 1 = metal

members.name: m_roughness
members.doc: 0 = smooth/mirror, 1 = rough/diffuse

members.name: m_ao
members.doc: Ambient occlusion (1 = no occlusion)

members.name: m_opacity
members.doc: 1 = opaque, < 1 = transparent

members.name: m_specularColor
members.doc: Legacy specular (for backward compatibility with non-PBR shaders)

members.name: m_metallicRoughnessTex
members.doc: Combined: R=metallic, G=roughness

members.name: m_opacityTex
members.doc: R = coverage (standalone cutout mask)

members.name: m_detailAlbedoTex
members.doc: overlay albedo

members.name: m_detailNormalTex
members.doc: overlay tangent-space normal

members.name: m_maskMapTex
members.doc: R=metallic, G=AO, B=detail mask, A=smoothness

members.name: m_heightTex
members.doc: R = height (0=surface, 1=deepest)

members.name: m_detailTiling
members.doc: UV multiplier for detail textures

members.name: m_detailAlbedoStrength
members.doc: 0..1 — blend amount over primary albedo

members.name: m_detailNormalStrength
members.doc: 0..1 — strength of detail normal influence

members.name: m_parallaxHeightScale
members.doc: POM displacement amount; 0.02-0.08 typical

members.name: m_displacementMagnitude
members.doc:
Meshlet-path geometric displacement from the height map, object-space
units; < 0 = not set here (an instance then takes its parent's; a root
reads 0 = off). No override bit is left in MaterialOverride, so the
sentinel is what carries "inherit".

members.name: m_displacementCenter
members.doc: height that stays put; < 0 = inherit / 0.5

members.name: m_clearCoatIntensity
members.doc: 0 = disabled, 1 = full lobe

members.name: m_clearCoatRoughness
members.doc: 0 = mirror coat (glossy), 1 = matte coat

members.name: m_anisotropy
members.doc: -1..1; 0 = isotropic GGX

members.name: m_subsurfaceStrength
members.doc: 0 = no SSS, 1 = max wrap

members.name: m_iridescenceIntensity
members.doc: 0 = no shift, 1 = full rainbow Fresnel

members.name: m_hair
members.doc: anisotropic Kajiya-Kay strand shading (hair/fur)

members.name: m_transmissionStrength
members.doc: TwoSidedFoliage back-light bleed, 0..1

members.name: m_sheenIntensity
members.doc: Cloth sheen lobe strength, 0..1

members.name: m_eyeParams
members.doc: Eye: transported by record, never by a GBuffer lane

members.name: m_graphParamsExt
members.doc:
Lanes 4.. of a graph whose parameters outgrew the legacy four (see
MaterialGraph::FGraphParam). Empty for every material that fits, so the
per-frame proxy copy of such a material costs exactly what it did.

members.name: m_reflective
members.doc: forward transparent reflection opt-in

members.name: m_physicsMaterial
members.doc:
What the surface is made of once something collides with it. The path
names a `.physmat`, which is where friction, restitution and the
surface type are already authored together; the inline name is the
fallback for a material that only wants to say "this is metal".

The surface is held as a NAME rather than the enum because ESurfaceType
lives in Physics, well above the renderer in the module order — the same
reason it serializes by name everywhere else.

members.name: m_parent
members.doc: null = base material

members.name: m_overrideFlags
members.doc: Which properties are overridden (All = standalone material)

types.name: Material
types.doc:
An instance can inherit from a parent material and override only specific
properties.

Ownership: a Material is RefCounted and lives behind Ref<Material>. Assets
(ModelResource, MaterialAsset) hold the Ref; a component's raw `Material*`
is a VIEW derived from a Ref somebody else holds, never an owner. The last
Ref to drop frees the material and, through it, its GPU texture refs —
exactly once, however many components shared it. Creation goes through
Create()/CreatePBR()/Clone(): every allocation AND the deleting destructor
below run inside the Renderer image, so a Ref released from any other DLL
frees through the same heap that allocated.

members.name: Material
members.doc:
A material is never copied as a value: the count belongs to one object.
Clone() is the field-wise duplicate; CopyFrom() writes another material's
surface into THIS one without touching its identity or its count.

members.name: Clone
members.doc:
New object, same surface: textures are shared by Ref, the parent pointer
is shared, the identity is fresh — the DS cache treats it as a different
material, which it is.

members.name: CopyFrom
members.doc:
Overwrites the surface with `other`'s. Keeps this object's identity and
its in-flight transparent-write depth, and never lets the texture
version step backwards: the DS cache keys on it, and a version that
re-reached an old value would hand back the old descriptor set.

members.name: ResetInPlace
members.doc:
Back to a default-constructed surface IN PLACE — the object, its address
and its identity survive, so every Ref and every view keeps working.
This is the reimport contract: an asset reloads its material's contents,
it does not replace the material. The texture version moves forward for
the same reason CopyFrom's does.

members.name: GetStateVersion
members.doc:
Moves on every write to the surface (any setter, CopyFrom, ResetInPlace,
ResetToParent), including writes inside an FTransparentWriteScope. It
says nothing about the parent: a cache that snapshots an instance must
also check the parent chain.

members.name: GetAverageTextureColor
members.doc:
Linear-space average of the albedo texture (white when untextured
or the average is unknown). The GI voxelizer multiplies the flat base
color by this — matching the GBuffer's baseColor * texture composition
at 1-texel resolution — so GI bounce and SDF/RT reflections carry the
texture's actual tint instead of the bare base color.

members.name: GetAverageTextureAlpha
members.doc:
Linear average of the albedo texture's ALPHA channel (1 when
untextured/unknown). For alpha-masked materials this is the cutout
coverage — the GI voxelizer dithers occupancy by it and the RT ray
queries use it as the stochastic any-hit accept probability.

members.name: IsTransparent
members.doc:
Translucent when the surface lets anything through OR when its blend
mode is not plain alpha: a FULLY opaque additive material (glow cards,
holograms) still has to leave the GBuffer and draw in the blended pass,
and inferring translucency from opacity alone silently made those
opaque.

members.name: SetBlendMode
members.doc:
How a translucent surface combines with what is behind it. Alpha is
the historical (and default) behaviour; Additive adds light (fire,
glows), Modulate multiplies (stained glass, smoked plastic). The RHI
has carried all three since G5 — this is the material-level choice
that was missing, so authors could only ever get alpha.

members.name: SetAlphaMasked
members.doc:
Alpha-masked (cutout) rendering — foliage/fences: the GBuffer and
shadow passes clip pixels whose albedo alpha falls below the cutoff
instead of blending. Independent of IsTransparent (which routes to
the blended pass).

members.name: SetDoubleSided
members.doc: Double-sided: rendered with backface culling off (leaf cards, cloth).

members.name: SetSpecularColor
members.doc: Legacy specular properties (for backward compatibility)

members.name: SetAlbedoTex
members.doc:
Instance inheritance: a texture setter marks its override flag, and
the getter falls back to the parent when this instance hasn't overridden
the slot — so an instance with no texture override renders the parent's
texture instead of nothing. Base materials (no parent) always use local.

members.name: SetOpacityTex
members.doc:
Standalone opacity/cutout mask — the DCC-FBX foliage convention, where
coverage lives in its own grayscale map instead of the albedo's alpha.
When bound, the masked passes clip against THIS texture's red channel
rather than the albedo's alpha (an opaque albedo would clip nothing and
leave the card a solid quad). Unbound = clip against albedo alpha.

members.name: SetDetailAlbedoTex
members.doc:
Detail maps — overlaid on primary albedo / normal at close range. Used
to add high-frequency surface detail without 4K source textures.
detailTiling multiplies the UVs (typically 4-8x). The overlay strength
is gated by the mask map's B channel when a mask map is set, so the
detail can be limited to specific regions (e.g. dirt-mask only on the
bottom half of a wall).

members.name: SetMaskMapTex
members.doc:
Mask map — single RGBA8 replaces metallic + AO + smoothness + detail
mask, packed HDRP-style:
R = metallic, G = AO, B = detail mask, A = smoothness (1 - roughness)
When set, the shader uses the mask map values instead of the scalar
metallic/AO/roughness in BaseColor/PBRParams. Saves descriptor slots
and bandwidth vs separate textures.

members.name: SetHeightTex
members.doc:
Parallax Occlusion Mapping. Height map is a single-channel R8 texture
where 0 = surface, 1 = deepest point. The shader ray-marches along the
tangent-space view direction to find the intersection with the height
field and displaces UVs accordingly — adds genuine 3D-looking detail
at silhouettes without changing geometry.

heightScale ~0.02-0.08 for typical floor/wall textures. Larger values
exaggerate but break at grazing view angles ("swimming texels"). The
shader uses adaptive step count (8-32) based on view-angle perpendicular-
ness to keep grazing angles sharp without wasting samples head-on.

members.name: SetClearCoatIntensity
members.doc:
Clear coat — a second specular lobe on top of the base BRDF, modeling
a thin transparent lacquer layer (car paint, painted wood, soda cans).
Fixed F0 = 0.04 (IOR 1.5 lacquer), per-material intensity scalar
attenuates the lobe. Clear coat roughness is independent of base
roughness — a rough base under a glossy coat is the classic look.

Intensity 0 disables the lobe entirely; 1 = full strength. Typical
values: 0.6-0.9 for shiny car paint, 0.3-0.5 for satin lacquer.

members.name: SetAnisotropy
members.doc:
Anisotropy — stretches the specular highlight along the surface tangent
(positive) or bitangent (negative). The signature look for brushed
metal, hair, vinyl records, satin. Zero = isotropic (standard GGX).

The lighting pass derives the tangent direction from screen-space
position derivatives — no per-mesh tangent texture support yet, so the
anisotropy direction approximately follows the surface's screen-space
U/V flow. For authored brush direction, a future iteration would store
a tangent map in G-Buffer or sample it here.

members.name: SetSubsurfaceStrength
members.doc:
Subsurface scattering — fakes the warm glow on the shadow-side of skin /
wax / foliage by softening the diffuse terminator and tinting with
albedo. Strength 0 = standard Lambert; 1 = full wrap with curvature.
Not real Jimenez-style blur SSS — this is a Penner-style curvature
approximation that costs only a fwidth + a few mul-adds per pixel.

members.name: SetIridescenceIntensity
members.doc:
Iridescence — thin-film interference giving hue shifts based on view
angle. Approximated as an HSV rainbow swept by NdotV, mixed with the
standard Fresnel by `intensity`. 0 = disabled. Used for soap bubbles,
oil slicks, peacock feathers, beetle wings.

members.name: SetHair
members.doc:
Hair shading model — switches the lighting pass to an anisotropic
Kajiya-Kay strand model (dual shifted specular lobes) instead of GGX, for
hair/fur cards. Mutually exclusive with iridescence in the GBuffer pack
(the hair flag rides the sign of the iridescence lane). Pair with a
negative Anisotropy so the highlight stretches across the strand width.

members.name: SetShadingModel
members.doc:
Explicit shading model (G2). DefaultLit doubles as "legacy auto":
GetEffectiveShadingModel derives Hair/Subsurface from the older
per-scalar knobs so every existing asset keeps its look without a
resave. IDs are the GBuffer wire format (RT3.A high 3 bits) — 0 MUST
stay DefaultLit, because impostors and material-less draws write a
zero alpha and must remain plain-lit.

members.name: SetTransmissionStrength
members.doc:
TwoSidedFoliage transmission: how much light bleeds through the
surface from behind, tinted by albedo. Only sampled when the shading
model is TwoSidedFoliage (it is that model's custom GBuffer lane).

members.name: SetSheenIntensity
members.doc:
Cloth sheen: how much of the Charlie retro-reflective lobe rides on top
of the base diffuse. It is the Cloth model's custom lane, so it only
reaches the GBuffer when the material asks for that shading model.

members.name: SetEyeParams
members.doc:
Eye's parameters. They reach the shader through the frame's
surface-parameter record, not through a G-Buffer lane, so they are only
read when the effective shading model is Eye.

members.name: HasAnyTexture
members.doc:
Uses the fallback getters so an instance counts textures inherited from
its parent (not just its own overrides).

members.name: SetTerrainSplat
members.doc:
Terrain splat: the GBuffer draws this material through the
TERRAIN_SPLAT pipeline — vertex color = 4 layer weights over the
albedo/detailAlbedo/detailNormal/maskMap image slots.

members.name: SetFoliageWind
members.doc:
Foliage wind: the GBuffer draws this material through the FOLIAGE
pipeline — vertex color alpha = bend weight, DetailParams repurposed
as wind direction/strength/speed (foliage has no detail maps).

members.name: SetWindParams
members.signature: void SetWindParams(const Vec2& direction, float strength, float speed)

members.name: SetReflective
members.doc:
Reflective translucent surface: the forward transparent pass casts a
single mirror reflection ray through the world SDF clipmap (shaded from
the radiance cache, sky on miss) and composites it Fresnel-weighted over
the glass. Off by default — a non-reflective transparent keeps the plain
ambient+refraction look (bit-identical). High/Epic + the
r.Reflections.Translucent cvar gate it globally. Clear-coat transparents
draw a coat reflection from the same source regardless of this flag.

members.name: SetWater
members.doc:
Water: the transparent pass draws this material through the WATER
pipeline — Gerstner vertex displacement + fresnel shading. The material
must also be transparent (opacity < 1) to reach that pass at all.

members.name: SetWaterWaveParams
members.signature: void SetWaterWaveParams(const Vec2& direction, float amplitude, float wavelength, float steepness, float speed)

members.name: SetWorldGrid
members.doc:
World grid: the albedo becomes the procedural grid and the albedo
texture is ignored. MaterialOverride has no bit left, so an instance
inherits the grid from its parent unless it switches it on itself.

members.name: kWorldGridAlbedoLane
members.doc:
The GBuffer push block's bindless-albedo lane names a table slot when it
is >= 0 and the per-material set at -1; this value below both selects
the grid, so no pipeline or push-constant byte had to be added for it.

members.name: PackWorldGridDetailParams
members.doc:
DetailParams of a grid draw: x = major cell, y = minor cell (metres,
clamped away from zero), z/w = major/minor line shades.

members.name: SetPhysicsMaterialPath
members.doc:
The physics surface. Empty on an instance means "whatever the parent
says": MaterialOverride has no bit left to spend on this, and an
instance that wanted to differ physically authors one of these fields.

members.name: HasAuthoredPhysics
members.doc:
Whether anyone authored a physics answer at all. A material that did not
has to leave the collider exactly as it was, which is what keeps every
scene predating this block behaving identically.

members.name: CreateInstance
members.doc:
The instance points at its parent but does not own it: whoever holds
the parent's Ref (its asset) must outlive the instance, as before.

members.name: CreateMetallic
members.signature: static Ref<Material> CreateMetallic(const Vec4& baseColor, float shininess = 64.0f)

members.name: CreatePBR
members.signature: static Ref<Material> CreatePBR(const Vec4& baseColor, float metallic, float roughness, float ao = 1.0f)

members.name: CreatePBRMetal
members.signature: static Ref<Material> CreatePBRMetal(const Vec4& baseColor, float roughness = 0.3f)

members.name: CreatePBRDielectric
members.signature: static Ref<Material> CreatePBRDielectric(const Vec4& baseColor, float roughness = 0.5f)

members.name: CreateWorldGrid
members.doc:
The engine default surface: a mid-grey world grid, rough dielectric.
Every mesh that has no material of its own draws with this.

members.name: SetGraphShaderId
members.doc:
Compiled material graph (UE5-gap Q1). A non-empty id names the
per-material GBuffer permutation in the shader archive
("Materials/<hex>"); GraphTextures carries the graph's slot-ordered
texture bindings for the material descriptor set. Empty id = the
classic uber-shader path, untouched.

members.name: GetGraphShaderHash
members.doc:
The id as the number it was printed from, so the renderer's ten graph
pipeline caches key on a word instead of rebuilding a 16-character
string per draw per pass per cascade — one character past MSVC's small
string buffer, so every one of those copies allocated.

members.name: HashGraphShaderId
members.doc:
The canonical id is "%016llx" of the graph's content hash, so parsing it
recovers that hash exactly and adds no collision the hash did not
already carry. Anything else — a hand-written id in a test — is folded
instead, which keeps it distinct without pretending it round-trips.

members.name: SetGraphHasWpo
members.doc:
G4: whether the graph links a World Position Offset. Drives the
shadow/velocity pipeline swaps — a no-WPO graph keeps the cheap uber
vertex path there (the pixel splice is independent of this flag).

members.name: SetGraphWpoBound
members.doc:
Conservative world-space bound on |WPO| from the graph compile (0 = no
WPO; a huge sentinel = unboundable subtree). The meshlet path inflates
its per-cluster cull spheres by it — or, at the sentinel, stops
trusting geometric kills for the draw entirely.

members.name: SetSubstrateTop
members.doc:
The graph's Substrate slab folded to one packed G-Buffer word, 0 when the
material has no slab or when its slab moves per pixel. Read by the paths
that cache ONE answer per surface and therefore cannot carry a per-pixel
coat: the GI surface cache's card capture and the ray-traced hit shading.
Everything that shades per pixel reads the slab out of the G-Buffer and
must ignore this.

members.name: SetGraphParamLane
members.signature: void SetGraphParamLane(uint32_t lane, const Vec4& v)
members.doc:
R4: the runtime parameter lanes the graph pipelines push per draw.
MaterialAsset seeds the graph's defaults and maps names to lanes;
gameplay writes lanes through it (SetScalarParameter/SetVectorParameter).
The first four lanes are the legacy block every graph pipeline reads;
a graph that needs more sizes the extension once at GPU-create time
(SetGraphParamLaneCount, from CompiledShader::paramLanes) and the
upload copies GetGraphParamLaneCount() lanes instead of four.

types.name: Material::FTransparentWriteScope
types.doc:
Writes that REPRODUCE a material rather than author it — the .mat
loader replaying a saved document, the graph compiler folding its result
onto the flat fields, a GPU re-resolve rebinding textures — must not read
as user edits. Inside this scope the setters still write their fields but
stop raising override bits, so an instance keeps inheriting exactly what
its stored mask says it inherits instead of freezing at whatever its
parent happened to hold the last time the file was opened.

types.name: FMaterialRenderProxy
types.doc:
Render-thread snapshot of a Material (+ its resolved parent chain), the
UE5 FMaterialRenderProxy analog. The game thread builds one per frame; the
render thread reads only this copy, never the live Material. Ref-counted so
the frame packet keeps it alive past the game thread freeing the source.

members.name: sourceKey
members.doc: original Material's stable id — DS-cache key across frames (0 = no material)

members.name: sourceVersion
members.doc:
FMaterialRenderProxyCache bookkeeping, read and written by the game
thread only (the render thread reads the fields above). They live on the
proxy so a holder that kept one across frames can prove it is still the
cache's current snapshot without a map lookup (Revalidate).

free.signature: inline MaterialOverride operator|(MaterialOverride a, MaterialOverride b)

free.signature: inline MaterialOverride operator&(MaterialOverride a, MaterialOverride b)

free.name: operator|=
free.signature: inline MaterialOverride& operator|=(MaterialOverride& a, MaterialOverride b)

free.signature: inline MaterialOverride& operator&=(MaterialOverride& a, MaterialOverride b)
